question: how do i check the battery level on my op-xy, and how should i charge it?
facts: Holding com makes the level meter light up with the approximate battery level.
It charges through the USB-C port on the right side, from a computer or USB charger.
To keep the battery healthy, charge it at least once every six months.

question: can the op-xy send cv/gate or clock sync to my modular gear, and at what voltages?
facts: The signals come from the 3.5 mm multi out jack, which works in one mode at a time: cv/gate, or a sync mode (sync8, sync16 or sync24).
The CV output range is ±5 V.
Sync and gate signals are output at 5.2 V.

question: what does pressing play or stop a second time do?
facts: Pressing play again while the pattern plays restarts playback from the beginning.
Pressing stop a second time silences every note and sound on the device.

question: what are the four numbered buttons under the screen for?
facts: The buttons labelled 1 to 4 are called M1, M2, M3 and M4.
They switch between the four modules, or sub-modes, of the current main mode.
Modules let you edit the selected track's parameters using the four encoders.
Arrange is the only main mode that has no modules.

question: the op-xy guide talks about combo presses, sequence presses and holds. what's the difference?
facts: A combo press means holding one key down and then pressing a second key.
A sequence press means pressing one key and then another, one after the other.
A hold means pressing a button and keeping it held down.

question: how do i start a new project, and what sounds are on the tracks by default?
facts: Pressing the project button brings up the project view.
From the project view, a long press on M1 creates a fresh project.
Out of the box, tracks 1 and 2 hold drums and track 3 holds a bass.
Tracks 4 to 8 are a pluck, a lead, a soft pluck, strings and a pad, in that order.

question: in a new project i have a kick on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 of track 1. how do i add a snare on 5 and 13 without disturbing the kick?
facts: In a new project the snare is on the G key, right next to the kick.
Hold the snare key and press record so the sequencer shows only the snare's steps.
Keep holding the snare key while pressing steps 5 and 13, then let go.

question: the bassline i recorded runs past the end of the pattern and overlaps itself. how do i lengthen the pattern, or clear it and start again?
facts: Holding bar and tapping [+] adds one more bar to the pattern.
Up to three extra bars can be added, making four bars in total.
For even longer patterns, hold bar and press accidental keys to raise the track scale, multiplying each step's length.
To erase the track, keep record and stop held until every step lights red.

question: what are the four main modes on the op-xy and what is each one for?
facts: Instrument mode is for composing; its track buttons edit the 8 instrument tracks.
Auxiliary mode is for transposing tracks and also covers send effects, external inputs/outputs and punch-in FX.
Arrange mode builds the song by chaining scenes made from the tracks' patterns.
Mix mode sets track levels and panning, plus the master compressor and main EQ.

question: how do i link tracks together on the op-xy, and what happens once they're linked?
facts: Hold one track button and tap the track buttons you want linked to it.
Up to four tracks can be linked together.
The held track becomes the primary and controls all of the linked tracks.
A linked track can still be played on its own when you are on it instead of the primary track.

question: how do i record notes live in real time instead of step by step, and can i get a count-in first?
facts: Hold record and press play to arm live recording.
Step 1 flashes red while it waits; recording starts once you begin playing the keyboard.
For a count-in, hold record, press play, then press play once more.
Press stop when you are done recording.

question: can i give one step its own filter setting that's different from the rest of the pattern?
facts: Hold the step and turn an encoder to store a parameter lock on that step.
When playback reaches that step, the parameter is set to the locked value.
All four modules accept parameter locks, but players do not.

question: how do i make my pattern longer than one bar, and can i copy the first bar instead of starting over?
facts: Hold bar and tap + to add a bar.
A pattern can use at most four bars.
Hold bar plus shift, then press +, to duplicate the current bar.

question: how do i put a step component on a few steps, and how do i take it off again?
facts: Hold shift and press the steps you want; the selected steps flash.
Still holding shift, press a natural key to choose a component; each has its icon printed on it.
Keep shift held and use an accidental key to set the component's value.
To remove it, hold shift, reselect those steps and press the same natural key again.

question: how can i get ratchets or fast rolls on my hi-hat steps?
facts: Use the multiply step component, which multiplies a step's triggers to create a ratchet.
Hold shift, select the steps, then press the natural key marked with the multiply icon.
Pick an accidental key to set how many trigs the step is split into.

question: how do i turn on the arpeggiator for a track and change its pattern and speed?
facts: On an instrument or auxiliary track, tap player to open it, then tap it again to turn it on.
Pressing player while holding shift switches the player style, e.g. to arpeggio.
Turn E2 (mid grey) to change the arp pattern, such as up, down, up/down or random.
Turn E1 (dark grey) to set the arpeggio speed.

question: how do i save my project, does it auto save, and how do i make a copy under a new name?
facts: Auto save is enabled by default; you can turn it off in project settings or system settings.
In the project view, M2 saves the project and stores a version in its versions folder.
Save as is shift + M2; you then type a name for the duplicated project.

question: how do i change my project's time signature, and which time signatures can i pick?
facts: Time signature lives in the project settings: press project, then M4 to configure.
Turn E1 (dark grey) to select the tempo page of the project settings.
Turn E2 (mid grey) to pick the setting, then E3 or E4 to change its value.
Besides 4/4, you can choose 3/4, 5/4, 6/8, 7/8 or 12/8.

question: how do i add swing to my beat, and what does the groove setting actually change?
facts: Press tempo, from any screen, to open the tempo screen.
Turn E3 (light grey) clockwise past centre for swing, or counter-clockwise for shuffle.
Turn E2 (mid grey) to choose the groove type.
Grooves change note timing and velocity, adding slight randomisation so the feel is more human.

question: what's the difference between patterns, scenes and songs, and how many of each can i have?
facts: Every track, instrument or auxiliary, holds up to 16 patterns (older documentation says nine).
A single pattern holds at most 120 notes.
A scene is the set of patterns playing across the tracks, and a project has 99 scenes.
A song plays scenes in order, and a project holds up to 14 songs.

question: how do I get a sidechain-style pumping effect on my bass track?
facts: Duck is part of the lfo module on M4; choose it as the lfo type with shift + M4.
Turning E1 picks the duck source: any of the 16 tracks, or the metronome for four-on-the-floor pumping.
Clicking E1 toggles whether duck reacts to audio or to note data.
E2 sets how strongly duck pulls down the track's volume.

question: how do I make a synth track play mono with glide between notes?
facts: Play mode sits on the shift layer of the envelope module, M2.
While holding shift on M2, turn E1 to choose poly, mono or legato.
Turning E2 on that page sets portamento, meaning how long notes take to slide into each other.

question: can I duplicate the sound on one track onto another track, then store it as a preset?
facts: Hold the source track's key and press M2 to copy its sound.
Hold the target track's key and press M3 to paste the copied sound onto it.
Holding a track's key and pressing M4 saves that track's current sound as a preset.

question: can I apply punch-in fx to just one track instead of everything, and record them?
facts: On an instrument track, hold shift and play keyboard keys to trigger punch-in fx.
Keys in the lower octave affect only the current track.
Keys in the upper octave affect all tracks in that group, percussion or melodic.
If you record while doing this, they are written to auxiliary track 2, the punch-in fx track.

question: how do I play and sequence an external synth over midi, and set which channel it's on?
facts: External midi gear is played from auxiliary track 3, the external midi track.
Connect the synth via USB-C or via the multi-out jack.
On M1, E1 chooses the midi channel, E2 the bank and E3 the program.
Eight midi CCs live on M2 and M3, and they can be tweaked, sequenced and recorded.

question: how do I swap the effect on fx i, tweak it, and feed fx i into fx ii?
facts: The two send effects, fx i and fx ii, are auxiliary tracks 7 and 8.
Hold shift and press the fx track's key, then use the encoders to choose a new effect.
M1 is where the selected fx engine's parameters are edited.
Inside fx i, hold shift and turn E4 to set how much of fx i feeds fx ii.

question: how do I start a new pattern on a track and flip between its patterns?
facts: Patterns are created in arrange mode, opened with the arrange key.
Select the track with its track key, then press M1 to add a new pattern to it.
Turn E4 to move through the patterns that already exist on that track.

question: how do I string my scenes together into a song that loops?
facts: From arrange mode, hold shift and press arrange to open song mode.
Hold shift and press the numbered accidental keys to enter scenes in order, like dialing a phone number.
Turn E1 to toggle looping, so playback returns to the first scene after the last one.

question: how do I mute and solo tracks while mixing?
facts: In mix mode, shift plus a track key toggles that track's mute.
Keep one or more track keys held down in mix mode to solo those tracks.
Muting acts on a track's notes rather than on its audio.

question: how can I turn all my drums down relative to my synths in one move?
facts: In mix mode, M4 opens the master page.
On the master page, E1 sets the percussion group level.
E2 on the master page sets the melodic group level.
Percussive engines like the drum sampler feed the percussion group automatically; synths and the sampler feed the melodic group.

question: how do i record a sample on the op-xy, and is there a limit on how long it can be?
facts: Pressing sample from any screen takes you straight into sampling.
Hold M1 to record; recording only begins once the input level crosses the threshold.
The record threshold is set with the white encoder (E4).
Samples can be at most 20 seconds long in every sampler.

question: how do i chop a drum loop into slices across the keys in the drum sampler?
facts: Hold the keyboard key that holds the sample and press M1 to open the slicer.
Turn the dark grey encoder (E1) to choose a slice mode: transient, even or tap.
Slices are spread across the keyboard automatically and set to choke one another.
In transient and even modes, the white encoder (E4) sets how many slices are made.

question: how do i use the op-xy as a midi controller for my daw, and what can i set up in that mode?
facts: Press com, then M2, to switch OP-XY into MIDI controller mode.
Hold shift and turn the dark grey encoder (E1) to set the MIDI channel it sends on.
Hold shift and turn E2 to switch the knobs between absolute (0-127) and relative output.
Holding shift and pressing com leaves controller mode and goes back to com.

question: i want to use the multi-out jack for cv/gate but the setting on the com screen won't switch. why?
facts: The multi-out mode is chosen by turning the light grey encoder (E3) on the com screen.
Multi-out cannot be switched while a cable is plugged into it: unplug it, change the mode, then plug it back in.

question: how do i switch the synth engine on one of my instrument tracks?
facts: In instrument mode, pick the instrument track whose engine you want to change.
Shift + M1 opens the synth engine list for that track.
Turn the dark grey encoder (E1) to scroll through the engines.
Clicking the encoder or pressing M1 confirms the chosen engine.

question: what does the ratio knob do on the axis engine?
facts: On axis, ratio is on the mid grey encoder (E2) and sets the pitch of one oscillator.
Ratio values from 0 to 50 act as a detune.
Ratio values from 51 to 100 step through ascending fifths.

question: how do i swap the effect loaded on the fx i send track for a different one?
facts: Enter auxiliary mode and select the fx i track.
Hold shift and press the fx i track button to open the effect list.
Scroll through the effects with the white encoder (E4).
Confirm the choice by clicking the encoder or pressing M1.

question: my op-xy keyboard plays every note at the same level no matter how hard i hit the keys. how do i turn on velocity?
facts: Press com, then M1, to open system settings.
Turn the dark grey encoder (E1) to reach the keyboard settings page.
With the velocity setting selected, turn the light grey encoder (E3) to change it.
Velocity can be set to off, soft (for gentle playing) or hard (for heavier playing).

question: how do i get my own wav samples from my computer onto the op-xy?
facts: Connect OP-XY to the computer first; MTP mode (com, then M4) only appears once it is connected.
On a Mac you need the field-kit app to access the drive.
Copy wav or aiff files into the 'samples' folder, e.g. its 'user' folder or your own subfolders.
Sample file names may only use alphanumeric characters plus -, # and space.

question: i want to mix my op-xy from an external midi controller. which CC numbers set a track's volume, mute and pan, and on which midi channel do i send them?
facts: Track volume is CC 7.
Track mute is CC 9.
Track pan is CC 10.
Each of these goes on the track's own MIDI channel: channel 1 for track 1 up to channel 16 for track 16.

question: can i change the tempo or switch scenes on the op-xy with midi CC messages from my daw?
facts: Tempo listens to CC 80, on any channel.
The CC 80 value is half the tempo in BPM, so 48 gives 96 BPM and only even tempos can be set this way.
Scenes can be changed by CC: 83 steps to the previous scene and 84 to the next one.
CC 85 picks a scene directly, and CC 82 does the same but waits before switching.

question: how do i factory reset my op-xy?
facts: Power the OP-XY off, then hold com while turning it back on to enter te boot.
In te boot, press T7 (track button 7) and go through the on-screen steps.
A factory reset wipes all user content and settings, so back up your projects first.
